- If sentiment is consistently positive or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative or shows recent decline, model often overcorrects upward; adjust downward bias, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a strong upward spike in history (e.g., >95), model frequently overestimates continuation; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overshoot.
- When true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast slope in early days of decline.
- If sentiment history shows no strong trend (flat or zero), model tends to overfit recent trend; apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from initial forecast, consider horizon-specific correction: early days (1–7) should be more conservative, later days (8–30) allow for gradual decay if sentiment remains neutral.
